description: We’re building an AI-powered fire safety dashboard for future Moon and Mars missions. In microgravity, flames act strangely: they turn into spheres, burn blue and spread in unexpected ways. NASA has decades of experimental data on this, but it’s scattered across hundreds of papers. Our plan is to turn that research into clear, searchable, source-cited safety insights that mission planners could actually use.
summary: FlameMind is an SI powered web application that turns NASA’s microgravity combustion research into clear, source cited fire safety insights for spacecraft, space stations, rovers and future Moon and Mars bases. It draws on the 24 combustion investigations in NASA’s Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database, which are hard to find, compare and interpret. Users can take two paths. On the Scenario page, they describe their design in plain language and get the relevant NASA data with citations, plus suggestions tailored to their use case. On the Explore page, they filter every investigation and test themselves, including custom filters for any parameter, with results shown as downloadable tables. FlameMind also shows where no experiment has been done yet, such as partial gravity. This matters because future lunar habitats will likely run at 30% oxygen or more, which makes materials far more flammable. FlameMind helps engineers and researchers choose safer materials, design better fire safety systems and plan the next experiments.
details:
The challenge. Fires in a spacecraft do not behave like fires on Earth. In microgravity, hot air does not rise, and flames can become spherical, soot-free, blue, and non-flickering. Future lunar habitats will use elevated oxygen, which makes everyday materials far more flammable. The measurements already sit in NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics repository: 24 Combustion Science investigations and about 12 terabytes. FlameMind, built by Team Spherical Flame for Flame in Freefall, is a lookup for those measurements. It does not replace the experiments, and it does not predict a flame size.

How it comes together. Ask → place the habitat → see what was never tested → read the control the record actually states.

  1. Ask. Scenario answers from the indexed records and names the PSI page for each number. A value the source does not state stays blank. The worked example is Moon-base crew quarters at 34% oxygen and 8 psi.
  2. Place the habitat. Home shows the presets from 21% to 34% oxygen with a NASA photograph. Rank orders investigations for ISS, a Moon base, a rover, a spacesuit, or Mars. The score is calculated from stated conditions. Gravity is a reason, not a hidden score. The Mars atmosphere is labeled assumed: it reuses the Moon base preset, 34% oxygen at 8 psi.
  3. See the gap. Gaps plots tests that state both oxygen and pressure. No investigation in this set was run at Moon or Mars gravity. LUCI and FM2 are the expected source of that data. E-FIELD Flames does not fill the gap. Compare reads investigations side by side and does not draw a fitted flammability line.
  4. Read the control. Controls stays with what the records state: BASS and FLEX for prevention, SAME page 57 for ionization detection of sub-micron smoke, and BASS quenching near 1 cm/s for suppression. Earth applications shows a sourced Earth use only when the record’s own text names it. In this build, that insight is BASS-II feeding fire-detection and suppression models.

    Source Code: https://github.com/ahanthota/FlameMindWebsite

FlameMind is a Python pipeline and API behind a Next.js site.

Web. Next.js 16, React 19, and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS 4. Charts use Plotly. Tests run in Vitest.

API. Python 3.11, FastAPI, and Uvicorn. Answers and custom filters call Vertex AI Gemini through the Google Gen AI SDK. NumPy holds the search embeddings. The service runs on Cloud Run.

Accounts. Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore. Guests can use every page. A signed-in chat is saved only for that account.

Pipeline. Python reads the NASA PSI records with pypdf, pdfplumber, and pandas. Pydantic checks the extracted records. Vertex AI Gemini drafts the structured investigations and builds the embeddings. The extracted JSON is what the site and the API read.

Checks. pytest for the pipeline and API, ESLint for the web app.
dataRefs: All 24 investigations, 352 publication rows, 27 documents, 24 overviews, and 10 experimental tables. The extracted layer has 1,652 test rows. The text index has 528 chunks from 68 files. The pipeline does not download the bulk archive, raw video, or files larger than 50 MB. Four records are marked reviewed, fourteen still need review, and no reviewer initials are stored. Pho
